bugs.title: Solenoid pulse is 1000 ms instead of 2500 ms
bugs.description: PULSE_MS is defined as 1000 on line 7, but the spec requires a 2500 ms HIGH pulse on D8. The pulse-end check on line 79 uses this constant, so every pulse terminates early; measured evidence shows pulses lasting 1000 ms (e.g. "pulse from 825 ms lasted 1000 ms, expected 2500 ± 150 ms") across all scenarios. The retrigger-ignore logic on line 69 is correct, but the wrong duration makes the core function wrong. 5 of 5 pulse(s) had the wrong length: pulse from 825 ms lasted 1000 ms, expected 2500 ± 150 ms. A trigger at 1.20 s came during this pulse, which must not change its length.

bugs.title: Blink toggles twice as fast as specified
bugs.description: The half-period constant HALF_MS is 500 (line 6), but the elapsed-time test on line 61 compares an 8-bit millis slice against HALF_MS, so a toggle fires every 500 ms and the lamp changes state twice per 1000 ms cycle. Measured evidence shows D12 toggled 8 times in a 2000 ms window starting at 245 ms (limit 5) and 16 times over the 8.00 s run, i.e. a 250 ms half-period rather than 500 ms. D12 toggled 8 times in a 2000 ms window starting at 245 ms (limit 5), and 16 times over the whole 8.00 s run.

bugs.title: Limit polarity inverted: motor disabled when limit is clear
bugs.description: Line 20 defines limitActiveRaw() as digitalRead(LIMIT_PIN) == HIGH, and line 69 sets hit = (stableLimit == HIGH), so the firmware treats a HIGH (clear) limit as active. The spec requires active = LOW, so D13 is driven LOW (line 74) while the limit is clear and HIGH while it is pressed, the exact inverse of the requirement. Measured: "D13 was not HIGH for 700 ms while required" and "D13 was not LOW for 48 ms while required" across 31 intervals. D13 was in the wrong state for 4842 ms across 31 interval(s), first at 100 ms: D13 was not HIGH for 700 ms while required (grace 100 ms).

bugs.title: Fan toggles far exceed the 2-per-5000 ms limit during button activity
bugs.description: The boost branch at lines 62-67 calls driveFan(true) on every 50 ms sample while D4 reads LOW, and the hysteresis branch at lines 87-94 calls driveFan(true)/driveFan(false) unconditionally whenever a hold counter reaches HOLD, with no check of the current fanOn state and no debounce or rate limiting. When the button is released the temperature logic immediately re-evaluates and can drive the fan back off, so each press/release cycle produces multiple D5 transitions; measured evidence shows 7 toggles in a 5000 ms window for button bounce, 8 for short clean presses, and 26 for rapid presses (limit 2). D5 toggled 7 times in a 5000 ms window starting at 1.00 s (limit 2), and 8 times over the whole 8.00 s run.
